data.name: Damodar
data.gender_notes: Damodar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Damodar is a name derived from Sanskrit, meaning 'one who holds the universe'. In Hindu mythology, Damodar refers to Lord Krishna, who holds the universe on his chest. This name is filled with spiritual significance and symbolizes love, compassion, and the power to hold and protect the universe. The name Damodar carries the meaning “Lord of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Damodar usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of love and protection, holding the universe
data.etymology: Damodar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Damodar total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Damodar signifies the 'one who holds the earth'. In Hindu mythology, Lord Krishna is referred to as Damodar, symbolizing his divine role in maintaining the cosmic balance and keeping the universe in order. The name also signifies the love and devotion between Lord Krishna and his consort, Radha.

vedic_reference.note: Damodar is a form of Lord Krishna, where he is depicted as the one who can be held in the palm.

historical_references.reference: Damodar River is named after Lord Krishna, who was once bound with ropes by his wife Satyabhama to prevent him from leaving her. The name Damodar means 'one who is bound with ropes'.

The name Damodar is also associated with the Damodar Valley Project, a hydroelectric power project in India, which was named after Lord Krishna in his avatar as Damodar. The project was completed in 1948.

modern_usage.modern_context: Damodar is a popular name in Hinduism, often referred to as the god of rivers and the god of abundance. In modern times, Damodar is celebrated and explored through various platforms. Religious tourists often visit temples dedicated to Damodar, particularly in India where the Damodar River flows. Devotional music, especially in the Bengali tradition, continues to be a significant part of Damodar's modern context. And, digital artists have created numerous works inspired by the stories, symbols, and aesthetics of Damodar, which can be found on platforms such as DeviantArt.
